# The Mandalay Bay: appendix {.page-title}

[Game inventory · save format · return disclosure]{.kicker}

Supporting material for [The Mandalay Bay case study](../degen-llms.qmd). Counts are the October 2026 snapshot and can move with content updates.

## Game inventory

| Surface | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Casino floor | 8 themed floors, table games, sports book, arcade, slots |
| Slot catalog | 37 machines |
| Trading floor | 744 stored contracts, 337 sports events, 204 prediction scenarios |
| Resort | Hotel, pool complex, dining, rewards programme |
| Pixel RPG | Walkable Strip overworld and hosted games |
| Save system | 5 slots; web save format version 8 |

## Save and clock rules

- The browser save, the terminal game and the RPG share one chip wallet. Play chips only; nothing is purchasable.
- The resort clock maps two real hours to one in-game day.
- The save stores lifetime totals; rewards tiers are recomputed on load, so a player who had maxed an old ladder can drop until they wager more.

## Randomness and returns

The fortune games report a return-to-player band of 155–185%, with every one of the 37 machines above 100%. That is deliberate for a play-money arcade, not a claim about real casino economics.

Randomness runs through `Math.random` in the browser build; the repository documents where it is called. There is no cryptographic RNG, no provable fairness and no real-money settlement.

## Snapshot boundaries

Test and line counts on the case study and report are dated and were not re-counted for this appendix. The deployed Pages build is manual, so the live demo can lag `main`.
